model.combined: Jump model + gradient boosting + onset detector (stress)
dash.dimension_help: Normalised score: 0 = historical average, ±1 = one standard deviation.
dash.states_rule: **The rule** labels each day from the three scores: **Stress / crisis** if stress is above {stress_threshold}; otherwise **Inflationary overheating** if inflation is above {inflation_threshold}; otherwise **Slowdown** if growth is below {growth_threshold}; otherwise **Expansion**.
dash.states_help: The model ({model}) groups days into states that have no name. Each state takes the name of the regime whose **centre** is closest to its own, a regime's centre being the average day the rule puts in that regime over the training period. Nothing is set by hand: two states can share a name, and a regime absent from history cannot name any state. The table shows the fit used on this date and the share of each state's days that the rule puts in the regime it is named after (agreement).
dash.states_none: This model predicts the rule regimes directly: it has no states to name.
dash.states_shares: How each state's training days split across the rule regimes. A state under 50% is a mixed state.
dash.states_cube: The three dimensions together: one dot every 5 days, colored by the rule regime; numbered diamonds = centres of the model's states; large dot = date shown.
dash.drivers_help: Each indicator in standard deviations from its own history (point-in-time).

disclaimer: General market information, identical for everyone. Not investment advice.
method.text: Data is turned into 12 point-in-time indicators (rolling windows, z-scores on the history available at each date, publication lags for monthly series), grouped into three dimensions: stress, growth, inflation. A transparent rule defines the 4 regimes from these three scores. The default model combines a statistical jump model (persistent regimes, causal filtering), whose states each take the name of the closest regime centre, with two fast models that raise the stress probability (gradient boosting one week ahead, stress-onset detector). Every probability shown is out of sample (walk-forward). Stress episodes are dated by a rule fixed before testing.

world.method: How the stress state is computed
world.method_text: This is not the macro regime (stress, growth, inflation), which exists only for the United States. For each country, from its ETF alone: **Stress** when 21-day realised volatility is in the top {stress_pct}% of its last 5 years **and** the drawdown from the 1-year high is beyond {dd}; **Elevated** when volatility is in the top {elevated_pct}%; **Calm** otherwise. A new state counts after {days} days in a row. Same thresholds for every country, set before looking at real data, computed only from data available each day.
